title: Command A+ from Cohere: Specs, Pricing and a Test Run
summary: Command A+ from Cohere is available through OpenRouter, with specs, pricing, and hands-on test results showing real-world performance.
body_markdown:
## Connecting Command A+ to automation workflows


You can connect it three general ways today, and the simplest is an HTTP request step that calls OpenRouter directly, because none of them needs a vendor-specific integration for Command A+.


Whichever you pick, settle first who owns the OpenRouter key: a key issued under a named person's account stops working when that person leaves, and the workflow stops with it. The three routes below run from least to most setup.


### Option 1: an HTTP request step


You need the OpenRouter chat completions address, an authorization header carrying an API key, and a request body that names the Command A+ model ID and passes the messages.


Store the key in the platform's secret or connection field, never pasted into the step itself, and issue it from a team account with a spending limit set.


When you want to see exactly what's sent and returned on a single, well-defined call, such as classifying a ticket or summarising a document, this route fits. The cost is that you parse the response and handle errors and retries yourself.


### Option 2: an AI step with an OpenAI-compatible provider


This route needs an AI step that accepts a custom provider, plus the OpenRouter base address, the same key, and the model ID entered as text. OpenRouter follows the OpenAI request format, so the step treats Command A+ like any other model.


If you already run several AI steps and want Command A+ to sit beside them, with prompts and outputs handled the way they are today, this route fits.


Check that the platform lets you type a model ID freely; if it restricts you to a fixed list, this route is closed.


Activepieces has nothing specific to Command A+; on a paid plan you can use your own provider key, so model spend lands on your own provider bill.


A platform that resells you its own model has picked yours and priced it before you opened the product, and Command A+ would never reach that menu.


On Activepieces the Plus plan is $20 a month, and with your own AI keys every AI step costs 1 credit while the model spend lands on your own provider account, so the cost per task you measure is Command A+'s own, at your rate.


The same setup is reachable from Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or any MCP client.


### Option 3: an MCP server


This route needs an MCP server, a service that exposes tools to a model, and a client that can call it. It fits only when the work is agentic, with Command A+ choosing among tools across several steps.


It carries the largest ownership burden, because the server holds its own credentials and permissions, and someone must be named to review them. For a straightforward comparison on cost and speed, it adds moving parts without adding information.
